The Contract
Three days after the World Cup semi-final. You lost by four runs. Then somebody posted a photo of you at a party at 3 AM the night before.
"CAPTAIN PARTIES, COUNTRY CRIES." Every channel. Every hour.
I had one drink. I left at midnight. Nobody cares.
A five-star hotel in Bandra, Suite 1104. Your agent said "a meeting that will save your captaincy". He didn't say who with.
Nikhil Arora. I fix images. Yours is broken. So is my client's.
The Board wants a family man. Sponsors want a love story. And the country wants to forgive you. Let's give them a wedding.
The bedroom door opens. Tara Kapoor. Three hundred million followers. Two flops in a row. Barefoot, holding an iced coffee.
So you're the cricketer. You're shorter on TV.
Let's be clear. I don't watch cricket. I don't understand cricket. I think a googly is a type of egg.
"A googly is a ball that lies to you. Like this meeting."
Match her.
"And I don't watch your films. We're even."
Cold.
"I'll teach you. Over dinner."
Too smooth?
Hm. Okay. Not completely boring.
One year. Married in public, strangers in private. Separate rooms. You attend her premieres, she attends your matches. Clause twelve: a quiet divorce after twelve months.
Clause seven: no falling in love. It ruins the timeline.
Sign it.
Save your captaincy.
"Clause seven is unnecessary. Trust me."
Sign, with a smile.
Read every page twice first.
Captains read the pitch.
Page nine has a handwritten line, in Tara's writing: "He must never meet my mother alone."
Wonderful. One more rule. Mine, not his.
My mother can never find out it's fake. Never. Promise me.
You just married a stranger for one year. And she's more scared of her mother than of the country.
